newsitem.title: USA: IMF puts off decision on gold sales until Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: IMF puts off decision on gold sales until Wednesday.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has put off until this week a decision on a controversial proposal to sell a small amount of its gold to help the world's poorest nations.
IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus said Friday's board discussions on ways to help the world's poorest nations were "extremely cooperative and constructive.
"We will continue in the same spirit to conclude the work of the executive board next Wednesday, September 18," he said in a brief statement.

IMF management, backed by the United States, Britain and most other member nations, has proposed selling five million of the fund's 104 million ounces of gold to help finance stepped-up assistance to poor countries.
But a few nations -- Germany, Italy and Switzerland -- have opposed the proposal, arguing in part that the IMF should not sell gold except in cases of extreme financial emergency.

International monetary sources, who declined to be identified, said last week that they did not expect a formal vote at the board on the proposal. Camdessus wants to avoid a bitter fight at the board and instead may seek a general understanding on the sale of gold if needed.
"It may well just be a matter of wording, with certain understandings just to save everyone's face," one source said.

That may mean a clear commitment by IMF member nations to find the necessary funding for helping poor countries, with an understanding that gold sales would be used if other financing alternatives did not prove adequate.
